### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**13** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via record_change (literal, a string literal in authoredFlowProbe; a string literal in probeTrigger))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `objectName (literal, 58 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `96a9957ae940f1e635f159074fb0574e94a55bb1` — the merge of head `5eea9771e798ea2b4519a8781cc60df60103af10` into base `3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 96a9957ae940f1e635f159074fb0574e94a55bb1 && git checkout 96a9957ae940f1e635f159074fb0574e94a55bb1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132 5eea9771e798ea2b4519a8781cc60df60103af10 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132 && git merge --no-ff 5eea9771e798ea2b4519a8781cc60df60103af10

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3e19223bf561694fdbb575dd2490847038916132` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c21d260c14e29b896a973f293f7c28d4b48dcca7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts + none

Face: narrowing (the paths decide no face; the `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` line on the PR body and the changeset does). The floor is every non-prose path of the diff, the five files above. No other file in the diff implements them; `authored-site-expression.test.ts` and `mcp-validate-expression.test.ts` are read as evidence for the pins. Read outside the diff, never reviewed: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (the flow walk, `check`, `checkFlowNullGuards`, `warnUnprovisionedAnchors`, `warnShadowedFieldReads`, `judgeFieldFormula`, the `formulaCycleIssues` call), `flow-cel-root-scope.ts` (`perWriteSnapshotEntrance`), `runtime-gate.ts` (`runRuntimeAuthoringRules`, `RuntimeStackContext`), `authoring-rules.ts` (the expression rule's `runtimeTypes`), `stored-expression-inputs.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts` (`readObjectForCaller`, `servedObjectDefinitionOf`), `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`, `packages/metadata-core/src/object-schema-fls.ts` and `object-schema-fls-references.ts` (the mask).

Inputs: card #33147 body and its 3 comments (triage 6863163129, claim 6864566168, dev report 6867633023; no ruling and no earlier review record is on the thread), PR #33168 body, file list (8 files) and net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on the head.

Check-runs on the head: 66 concluded, 56 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (read 2026-11-14T00:02Z). Success includes Build Core, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), every Lint family, Test Core 8/8, Test UI 16/16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build and E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard. The 10 skipped are opt-in or queue-only jobs (Queue verdict, Borrowed queue verdict, Build Docs, packed-tarball smoke, 18.x upgrade harness, Temporal Conformance, UI Published Artifacts, Dogfood Verify CLI, the sharded dogfood matrix, the schedule gate).

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **`flow_condition`, record-triggered flow, unguarded nullable `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` read: `ok: true` on main, now `ok: false`.** RIGHT. It is `checkFlowNullGuards`, run by the gate's own walk on the probe's one edge (`afterStart: true`); the runtime flow door runs the same call on an edge and a `decision` branch, and with `afterStart: false` on the start node, which answers alike when the probe carries no start condition. Nothing is re-implemented: the entry calls `runStackExpressionPasses` with `runtimeWriteType: 'flow'`, the value `runRuntimeAuthoringRules` hands the expression rule on a flow write.
2. **`flow_condition`, any flow bound to an object, a `record.` / `previous.` read of an external object's unprovisioned injected column: no warning on main, now the gate's warning.** RIGHT. `warnUnprovisionedAnchors` rides `check` at every object-bound flow predicate, at both doors.
3. **`formula` with `field` naming a served stored field: now the `storedExpressionInputIssues` warnings.** RIGHT. The declared definition is kept and only `expression` is written over it, so the gate's own test (`type !== 'formula'` and an `expression`) decides.
4. **`formula` with `field` naming a served formula: now the `formulaCycleIssues` refusal on that field.** RIGHT. The field sits in the object's formula graph under its own name; only the finding located on that field's `expression` is kept.
5. **Is anything refused that the gate accepts?** Not for a call that describes its flow. Two defaults can refuse what the door accepts when the caller leaves the context out, and both are stated in the input descriptions: `triggerKind` defaults to `record_change` (as on main), and an omitted `startCondition` judges the condition as the start condition, so an edge after a guarding start is refused until `startCondition` is passed. The second is new on this head and is the BREAKING arm the changeset declares.
6. **Does anything the gate refuses still answer `ok`?** Against the runtime flow door, no refusal is left out that the tool could give: the bare-name null guard and the unbound-root refusal stand down there (`perWriteSnapshotEntrance`, rulings `5791822697` item 3 and `6104584601` as cited in `flow-cel-root-scope.ts`), and the probe follows by construction. Against `os validate` (the build door), `days` compared to 3 and an unbound root still answer `ok`; this is declared in the tool description, the skill line and the changeset. Note that the card's own example is the bare `days` compared to 3, which therefore still answers `ok` (see ③, flag 2).
7. **One warning the runtime flow door gives is not given by the tool and is described wrongly** (finding F1 in ④): the shadowed-field-read warning. It changes no `ok`.
8. **Sites `validation`, `formula` without `field`, and `template`: unchanged.** RIGHT. The `validation` and unnamed-`formula` branches build the same stack as on main; `template` has no `gatePasses`.
9. **New refusals of the two inputs on a site they do not describe** (`startCondition` off `flow_condition`, `field` off `formula`): RIGHT, the same shape as the existing `severity` / `triggerKind` / `sweepObject` refusals; no call valid on main is affected, since neither key was accepted before (unknown keys are refused by `strictToolInput`).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@object-ui/console`, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. This matches AGENTS.md step 3: `Metadata-protocol: none`, a non-protocol change ships `patch` whether widening or breaking, and keeps the banner and the disposition. RIGHT.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is on the PR body and the changeset body, line-initial, with `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it and a `Skills-docs: none — REASON` line on the PR body. One arm, the stricter one; the widening (the two inputs) is stated in the same line's prose. RIGHT. The claim comment predicted `no (narrowing)`; the diff does move a public surface (two MCP inputs, three lint exports), so `yes` is the accurate value.
- `@objectstack/lint` public entry: adds `AUTHORED_FLOW_NAME`, `AUTHORED_CONDITION_ID` and the type `AuthoredFlowTrigger`; `AuthoredExpressionSite` gains `'flow_condition'`; `AuthoredSiteExpression` gains four optional keys. All additive, and all named in the changeset. `authoredFlowProbe` is exported from the module only, not from the package entry. No export is removed or renamed.
- MCP inputs: `startCondition` and `field` are both `.optional()`; a call without them reaches the same code path as on main at `validation`, `formula` and `template`. Additive.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author login: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay; attribution `os-tesla`, dev session `session_01L9qibxiHaRMZVvPqb3cEac`, branch `claude/project-thread-ye3s0h`). The PR is a draft.

1. Dev report: `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []`. Nothing to answer. The diff stays inside the claim's file surface.
2. **Two decisions are attributed to the seat and have no record on the card thread** (should-fix, process): "The seat chose the runtime flow publish door" and "there is no `fieldType` input (seat ruling)". Both shape the contract: the first is why the card's own example (`days` compared to 3, bare) still answers `ok`, the second is why a stored field that is not declared yet gets no stored-expression warning. I judged both on the tree and find them sound (① item 6; the bare-name judgment needs the flow's variables and entrances, and a probe that declares none would refuse a name a real flow rebinds). The seat should put both rulings on the card before ACCEPT, and say there that the card's example is answered by the `record.FIELD` spelling.
3. Card item "whether to add a `field` input is the implementer's to propose": proposed, built, declared as the widening. Answered.
4. Triage note "the formula-cycle item may need an optional `field` input; that is a contract widening, so the PR declares it": declared. Answered.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts`** — holds.
- The probe is the smallest flow on which the door's walk reaches the three calls it makes at an edge. The slot filter is the edge's key path `flows[0].edges[0].condition`, which the walk stamps on every finding of a top-level edge, so the start condition's own findings and every finding on the objects are dropped.
- `objects: [body, ...others]` strips the injected system columns as the #33134 branches do; `RuntimeStackContext.objects` is declared "as authored", so the door reads the same shape.
- `withAuthoredFormulaField` reads the declared field with an own-property test and a record test, in both the map and the array form.
- **F1, should-fix.** The module header says the runtime door "never judges ... a read a flow variable shadows". The tree says otherwise: `warnShadowedFieldReads` runs at the start, `decision` and edge slots with no stand-down on a runtime write, and it reads only the written flow's own declared variables, which a per-write snapshot does carry. So a flow saved through MCP that declares a variable named like a field of its object, and reads that name bare in a condition, gets this warning at the door and none from the tool. The tool cannot give it (it is handed no variables), so the fix is the wording: say the door gives it and the tool is not handed what it needs. The test's own reason for this row is accurate; the header, the handler's jsdoc and the changeset sentence are not. No `ok` moves.

**`packages/lint/src/index.ts`** — holds. Three additive exports, named in the changeset.

**`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`** — holds, with F1 and F2.
- Fence and mask: `guard(objectName)` runs first, as before. The subject is read through `servedObjectDefinitionOf`, the same per-caller read `describe_object` projects, and at a flow condition no other object is read (`hops` is empty), which a pin holds. `sweepObject` only labels the probe's trigger; its definition is never fetched.
- `field` resolves in the served definition and nowhere else. I tried to tell a masked field from an absent one and could not: the mask removes the field and every reference to it (a readable formula that reads it loses its `expression`), so the formula graph the cycle pass walks carries no edge into the hidden name; a stripped system column and a masked one produce the same stack; the validator half does not read `field`. Masked, absent and no `field` answer alike, and a tool-level pin holds that over three expressions.
- No record is read: the handler calls `describeObject`, `optionFieldsOf` and `servedObjectDefinitionOf` only.
- F1 applies to the `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP` jsdoc ("that door does not give them").
- **F2, should-fix.** The `site` input still says "flow_condition binds fields bare" and the tool description still says "(fields are bound bare in flow conditions)", while the new sentence says to write `record.FIELD` to be judged. Both spellings bind, but an agent that follows the first gets `ok` on exactly the read the null guard exists for. Say in the `site` description that both bind and that only the `record.` spelling is null-judged here.
- Nit: `startCondition` is not validated itself; a malformed one proves nothing and says nothing. The PR body states that its findings are not reported.
- Nit: the `field` pattern admits `__validate_expression__` and `__proto__`; both are handled as plain own keys and judged as a new formula.

**`packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts`** and **`ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts`** — hold. The `validate_expression` entry is byte-identical in the two files at this head (compared as extracted text, 33 lines). It agrees with the tool: the two inputs, the `record.` / `previous.` null guard on a record-triggered flow, the anchor warning at three sites, the stored-field warnings, the door named, and "a field not yet declared is judged as a new formula". It names `os validate`'s bare-name and unbound-root judgments only, which is accurate.

Observation, outside this diff: the validator half of the tool has never been handed a flow's variables (`flowVariables`, `bareNamesUnproven`), so its type verdict on a bare name can differ from the door's on a flow that rebinds the name. It predates this PR; it belongs on a follow-up card with F1's gap.

Findings: F1 should-fix, F2 should-fix, ③ flag 2 should-fix (process), two nits. No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-ye3s0h`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibzuZJBQY4wUQFJbkfx`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5eea9771e798ea2b4519a8781cc60df60103af10`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/lint/src/authored-site-expression.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts, packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts, packages/mcp/src/skill-md.ts, ui/apps/console/src/pages/developer/objectstack-skill.ts + none

Delta round on record 6868101966 (head `c21d260c`, PASS with F1, F2 and one process flag). This head is that one plus a single commit, `5eea9771`. Judged: `git diff c21d260c..5eea9771` (3 files, 17 insertions, 13 deletions), the net diff against `main` where the delta touches it (the same 8 files as before), card #33147 with its 4 comments (the new one is the seat's rulings, 6868118121), and the check-runs on this head. Everything the first record judged and the delta does not touch stands as judged there.

Check-runs on the head: 66 concluded, 56 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending (read 2026-11-14T01:07Z). The same 10 opt-in or queue-only jobs are skipped as on the previous head.

### ① Derived judgments

The delta moves no accept set. Its hunks are:
- `authored-site-expression.ts`: the module header comment only (lines 34 to 41). No statement changes.
- `mcp-http-tools.ts`: the `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP` jsdoc, one parenthesis in the tool description string, and the `site` input's `.describe()` string. No schema shape, no handler statement, no refusal changes.
- the changeset: one paragraph.

So the commit is prose only: comments, two description strings and the changeset. The two strings are served bytes (an agent reads them in `tools/list`), but they change no verdict of any call. Every derived judgment of the first record (items 1 to 9) holds unchanged on this head. Item 7 is now declared, see ④.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still right: `patch` on the three packages, the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 marker, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and the changeset. The delta adds no export and no input. The changeset paragraph it rewrites stays inside the same declaration.

### ③ Boundary flags

PR author login: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay; attribution `os-tesla`). The PR is still a draft.

- The process flag of the first record is answered. Comment 6868118121 puts both seat rulings on the card: the runtime flow publish door as the gate the tool matches, with the consequence stated that the card's own bare example still answers `ok`; and no `fieldType` input, with its reason. It also records `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, which settles the difference from the claim's predicted `no (narrowing)`.
- No new dev flag and no open question arrived with this head.

### ④ Design judgment

**F1, closed.** Each of the three places now says what the tree does:
- the lint header: the door "does warn on a bare read of a name a flow variable shares with a field (`warnShadowedFieldReads`)", the entry is handed no variables, "the probe declares none and that warning never fires here", and an empty answer is the door's verdict "short of the shadowed-read warning". Accurate: `warnShadowedFieldReads` runs at the start, `decision` and edge slots with no stand-down on a runtime write and reads the written flow's own declared variables; `authoredFlowProbe` builds a flow with no `variables`.
- the `VALIDATE_SITE_MAP` jsdoc: the bare-name null guard and the unbound-root refusal are the two the door does not give; the shadowed-read warning is named as one the door gives and the tool cannot. Accurate, for the same reason, and consistent with `perWriteSnapshotEntrance` for the first two.
- the changeset says the same in one sentence.
The lint test's reason for this row already said so and is unchanged.

**F2, closed.** The tool description's parenthesis now reads "read fields as `record.FIELD` there too", and the `site` input says every site reads fields as `record.FIELD`, that a bare field name also resolves in a flow condition, and that this tool cannot judge its null guard there. Accurate against the handler: `flow_condition` keeps `scope: 'flattened'`, so both spellings resolve in the validator; the null guard the probe gives is on `record.` and `previous.` reads only. The description no longer steers an agent to the spelling the tool is blind to.

**`skill-md.ts` and the Console mirror**: untouched by the delta, still byte-identical to each other on this head (same extracted text as before), and still in agreement with the tool description after the two string changes.

**`index.ts`**: untouched.

One nit, new: "Every site reads fields as `record.FIELD`" is slightly wide for a flow that no record starts (a schedule flow binds no `record`; `os validate` refuses that root there, the runtime door and the tool do not). It has no effect on any verdict and the sentence is right for every flow the null guard applies to.

The two nits of the first record (`startCondition` is not validated itself; the `field` pattern admits `__proto__` and `__validate_expression__`, both handled as own keys) are left as they were, which is acceptable.

Findings on this head: no must-fix, no should-fix, three nits.

## 维护者速读 · PR #33168 @ `5eea9771` · 2026-11-14T01:10Z

- 改了什么：MCP `validate_expression` 在 `flow_condition` 上给出与运行时 flow 发布门同一个结论：记录触发的流程里未做空值保护的 `record.<字段>` / `previous.<字段>` 现在回 `ok: false`，外部对象未落库的注入列给出同一条警告。`formula` 站点可以用新的可选 `field` 指名一个已提供的字段，得到存储表达式的警告和公式环的拒绝。另有可选 `startCondition`。
